answer.worked:
Let $t=\tan\theta$. The equation is undefined at $\theta=\frac\pi4,\frac{3\pi}4$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{1-t}{1+t}&=\frac{3(1+t)}{1-t}\\(1-t)^2&=3(1+t)^2\\1-2t+t^2&=3+6t+3t^2\\2t^2+8t+2&=0\\t^2+4t+1&=0\\t&=\frac{-4\pm\sqrt{12}}{2}=-2\pm\sqrt3\end{align*}$$
For $\tan\theta=-2+\sqrt3$, $\theta=\frac{11\pi}{12}$. For $\tan\theta=-2-\sqrt3$, $\theta=\frac{7\pi}{12}$.

The substitution excludes $\theta=\frac\pi2$; substituting gives $-1\ne-3$, so it is not a solution.

Therefore $\theta=\frac{7\pi}{12}$ or $\frac{11\pi}{12}$.

Let $t=\tan\theta$. The equation is undefined at $\theta=\frac\pi4,\frac{3\pi}4$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{1+t}{1-t}+\frac{t-1}{1+t}&=2\sqrt3\\\frac{(1+t)^2-(1-t)^2}{(1-t)(1+t)}&=2\sqrt3\\\frac{4t}{1-t^2}&=2\sqrt3\\4t&=2\sqrt3-2\sqrt3t^2\\\sqrt3t^2+2t-\sqrt3&=0\\t&=\frac{-2\pm\sqrt{4+12}}{2\sqrt3}=\frac{-2\pm4}{2\sqrt3}\\t&=\frac1{\sqrt3}\ \text{or}\ -\sqrt3\end{align*}$$
For $\tan\theta=\frac1{\sqrt3}$, $\theta=\frac\pi6$. For $\tan\theta=-\sqrt3$, $\theta=\frac{2\pi}3$.

The substitution excludes $\theta=\frac\pi2$; substituting gives $-1+1=0\ne2\sqrt3$, so it is not a solution.

Therefore $\theta=\frac\pi6$ or $\frac{2\pi}3$.
